speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Patient
text: includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis. The combination of blisters on the forearm and mucosal ulcers, alongside the mention of pernicious anemia and Graves' disease (potential drug triggers), is highly indicative of a severe drug reaction. Given the urgency, please seek immediate emergency care or stop taking any new medications immediately.
